source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-10-09, from the ABFM 2025 In-Training Examination critiques, items 64 to 75. Each question cites its item. Authoring batch for the ITE pool; review before trusting.

questions.q: Irregular periods, a year of infertility, BMI 29. Which raised hormone most supports polycystic ovary syndrome?
questions.why: Hyperandrogenism can also be clinical: hirsutism, androgenic alopecia, acne. Insulin resistance is part of the pathophysiology but not of the criteria.

questions.q: Two of which three findings make the Rotterdam diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome?
d: A raised LH to FSH ratio
questions.why: Only after the mimics are excluded: androgen-secreting tumours, Cushing syndrome, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, thyroid and prolactin disorders among them.

questions.q: In a woman being evaluated for polycystic ovary syndrome, what does a raised 17-hydroxyprogesterone suggest?
questions.why: A raised cortisol points the other way, to Cushing syndrome or an adrenal tumour. Both mimic the syndrome and both must be excluded before it is diagnosed.

questions.q: Thirty-six hours of continuous vertigo, veering left, no hearing loss, a saccade on head impulse. What is next?
questions.why: Vestibular neuritis, probably viral, settling in days. Antiemetics for up to three days; vestibular rehabilitation if it lingers. Steroids and antivirals have not shown benefit.

questions.q: Which features point to vestibular neuritis rather than positional vertigo?
a: Continuous vertigo for more than a day
Listing to one side when walking
d: Brief spells brought on by head movement
questions.why: Positional vertigo is brief and triggered, and it gets the Epley manoeuvre. Hearing loss and tinnitus belong to neither; they are reasons to image.

questions.q: When is MRI of the brain indicated for vertigo?
d: Any vertigo lasting over a day
questions.why: Vestibular neuritis peaks between 30 and 50 and is a bedside diagnosis: nystagmus towards the affected side and a corrective saccade on head impulse.

questions.q: Melasma persisting six months after delivery. Which topical treatment is most effective?
d: Azelaic acid as used for acne
Imiquimod cream three times a week
questions.why: The three can be prescribed as one formulation, which is expensive, or separately. Azelaic acid and benzoyl peroxide are acne drugs; imiquimod is for warts.

questions.q: What proportion of melasma of pregnancy resolves after delivery?
questions.why: It affects up to three quarters of pregnancies, driven by oestrogen, progesterone and melanocyte-stimulating hormone, and can return with later pregnancies or the pill.

questions.q: Parents with egg and peanut allergies in the family ask when to introduce those foods. What is advised?
questions.why: Early exposure gives the lowest risk of later allergy. Eggs are cooked well.

questions.q: How is peanut introduced to an infant?
questions.a: Peanut butter thinned with water or milk
d: A skin-prick test first, for every infant
Peanut flour after the first birthday
questions.why: Breast milk, formula or cow's milk all serve to thin it. Whole peanuts are a choking hazard at any age in infancy.

questions.q: The day after a sexual assault, pregnancy test negative, STI tests sent. What is given empirically?
questions.why: Cover for gonorrhoea, chlamydia and trichomonas, with tinidazole as the alternative to metronidazole. Hepatitis C prophylaxis is not recommended.

questions.q: HIV post-exposure prophylaxis after a sexual assault is what regimen?
d: A single dose of two drugs
questions.why: The two-drug combinations are pre-exposure regimens and do not serve after an exposure.

questions.q: Which are options for emergency contraception after an assault?
questions.why: Long-term contraception can be offered afterwards, but emergency contraception comes first, along with the forensic examination if she wants it.

questions.q: Premenstrual low mood and irritability on fluoxetine 60 mg; the combined pill made it worse. What is added?
questions.why: Calcium levels cycle in premenstrual syndrome, though the mechanism is unknown. Bupropion has not shown benefit, vitamin D is not low in these patients, and low-dose dutasteride does nothing.

questions.q: Which are first-line treatments for premenstrual dysphoric disorder?
questions.why: High-dose dutasteride does relieve symptoms but harms mood and is teratogenic. Acupuncture has insufficient evidence.

questions.q: T-score minus 2.8. Alendronate was stopped after four weeks for gastric symptoms. What now?
questions.why: Provided it was taken correctly: empty stomach, a full glass of water, upright for thirty minutes. Raloxifene is not the preferred next step.

questions.q: Bacterial meningitis confirmed on lumbar puncture. Besides antibiotics, which intravenous drug improves mortality?
questions.why: It also reduces neurological sequelae. Acyclovir is for suspected herpes encephalitis, glycerol increased deaths in adult trials, and immunoglobulin is not a treatment.

questions.q: When is dexamethasone given in bacterial meningitis?
questions.a: Just before or with the first antibiotic dose
d: Once the culture result is back
If the fever persists at 48 hours
After the lumbar puncture, on day 2
questions.why: The benefit depends on the timing. A septic patient also needs fluid, which rules out a diuretic in the first hours.

questions.q: What is the empiric antibiotic regimen for bacterial meningitis in a 27-year-old?
questions.why: Bactericidal drugs also reduce the inflammation. The vancomycin covers resistant pneumococci until the sensitivities are known.

questions.q: Eosinophilic oesophagitis on biopsy, partial relief from a proton pump inhibitor. What is most likely to help?
questions.why: A swallowed inhaled steroid is the alternative. Famotidine suits erosive oesophagitis, montelukast is weaker here, and Candida oesophagitis would get fluconazole.

questions.q: Eosinophilic oesophagitis is confirmed above how many eosinophils per high-power field?
questions.why: With other causes of eosinophilia excluded. Rings, grooves and white exudates at endoscopy suggest it; the biopsy makes it.

questions.q: In what proportion of eosinophilic oesophagitis does a proton pump inhibitor alone give complete relief?
questions.why: Think of it in an atopic man in his twenties or thirties with years of dysphagia; more than half have had a food impaction.

questions.q: Crohn disease on methotrexate and azathioprine, age 45, Tdap six years ago. Which vaccine is given today?
questions.why: Inflammatory bowel disease is an indication at any adult age. MMR is live and contraindicated once immunosuppression has started, and the tetanus booster is not due for four years.

questions.q: Adrenal insufficiency, an infection, days of vomiting, BP 97/58, sodium 133, potassium 5.8, glucose 60. First drug?
questions.why: Adrenal crisis, which kills untreated. Glucagon treats insulin hypoglycaemia and does nothing for the circulation; the antiemetic treats a symptom.

questions.q: What is 1 mg of dexamethasone used for?
questions.a: A screening test for cortisol excess
questions.why: Dexamethasone can treat adrenal crisis but is not the preferred drug, and at this dose it is far below treatment.

questions.q: Which can precipitate an adrenal crisis in someone with known adrenal insufficiency?
questions.why: The picture is weakness, abdominal pain, tachycardia and hypotension, with low sodium, high potassium and sometimes low glucose.

questions.q: Which test is added to the syncope work-up when the episode occurred during exertion?
questions.why: With a normal examination, EEG, carotid imaging and head imaging are all not recommended. Fainting while standing in a queue is not exertion.
